subject: Scheduling: Dedicated capacity sizing call / next steps

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@fintechco.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Great call — propose a dedicated capacity sizing session

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for a productive discovery call this morning. Quick recap of what I heard:
- Primary use case: near-real-time customer support assistant (chat + retrieval) and nightly batch embedding jobs for search ranking.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 250ms for chat generation during peak windows.
- Expected concurrency: ~120 qps during peak for chat; batch jobs are ~10M docs/day (run overnight).
- Data constraints: PCI-adjacent, would prefer Private/Dedicated with VPC and KMS.

Next step: a 30–45 minute dedicated capacity sizing call with our Solutions Engineer to map those numbers to GPU sizing, expected throughput, and a rollout plan. Camila (cc'd) will lead the sizing.

Proposed agenda (30 mins):
1) Confirm traffic profile and request mix (chat vs embedding vs batch) — 8 mins
2) Throughput/latency targets and SLA questions — 8 mins
3) Mapping to instance types / dedicated pool sizing and cost ballpark — 10 mins
4) Next steps & mutual action plan — 4 mins

Available slots (PST):
- Tue 29 Jun, 10:00–10:45
- Tue 29 Jun, 14:00–14:45
- Wed 30 Jun, 09:00–09:45

If none of those work, happy to take a slot from your calendar (https://cal.com/marissa/redwood-30m).

Also attaching a short template to capture throughput numbers and sample payload sizes — if you can fill that before the call it will speed things up.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — that agenda looks good.

Quick answers:
- Our chat traffic: ~70% short conversational queries (avg token out 80–120), 30% multi-turn troubleshooting flows (avg token out 300–500).
- Burst tolerance: we need short bursts to 180–200 qps for marketing spikes.
- Batch: nightly embedding job is flexible (can stretch to 6–8 hours window if that helps).
- Security: we will need VPC and customer-managed keys; can provide SOC2 report and some compliance docs on request.

We can do Tue 29 Jun, 14:00 PST. Priya (cc) will join for security/infra questions.

Would be helpful if Camila can call out recommended instance types for the 95p <250ms target vs a cost-optimized configuration.

Appreciate it — see you tomorrow.

—Alex

Hi Alex — thanks for the details and for confirming the slot. I'll join the 14:00 PST call.

Prep ask (if possible before the call):
- Sample 1-minute traffic profile CSV (qps timeline for a typical peak hour) — helps size burst capacity.
- Average request payload sizes (prompt + context) and average response token counts for chat and batch sample sizes.
- Any preferred cloud telemetry or monitoring integrations (CloudWatch / Datadog / Prometheus).

I'll prepare two sizing scenarios for the meeting:
A) Performance-focused: target 95p <250ms with ~200 qps burst capacity (recommendations will include GPU types, KV cache sizing, and expected concurrent workers).
B) Cost-optimized: best-effort 95p ~300–400ms with lower reserved capacity and autoscale suggestions.

Also attaching a short Redwood dedicated overview PDF so you have rough SLA/pricing context before we meet.

See you at 14:00 PST.
